_comment: Where a scaffold lands. Everything this operation produces is written into ONE repo — the site being scaffolded — and that repo is not the one a factory session is usually standing in. A tree created and never committed is the failure mode: it survives the session, it is invisible in the factory's own git status, and the next session finds half a site nobody remembers creating.

places.root: the site repo named by the user
places.close: commit — one commit, in that repo's own terms
places.why_enter: The scaffold is the repo's first structural commit and the thing every later session builds on. Left uncommitted it is indistinguishable from a tree someone abandoned.

order: site (scaffold, run scripts/check_content.py, then commit — in that order)
_order_why: Committing a tree the validator has not seen commits the gaps too, and the first run is the one that catches a language folder that was declared and never created.
